value.reason: The Evidence shows an authentication token being saved in localStorage under the key 'token' in four separate flows: login.component.ts:150, oauth.component.ts:52, payment.component.ts:233 and two-factor-auth-enter.component.ts:54. request.interceptor.ts:16 then reads it back to build the 'Authorization: Bearer' header for every request. This is the same pattern as the positive SEC-10 example. localStorage keeps data after the browser closes and any script on the same origin can read it, including script injected through XSS, so an attacker could steal the session token. Nothing in the Evidence limits that access, such as an HttpOnly cookie, short-lived in-memory storage or encryption. That fits CWE-922 (sensitive data stored without limiting who can read it) and falls short of the security safeguards required by DPDP Rule 6(1)/6(1)(a). CWE-614 does not apply because no cookies are involved.
